tour.name: Kyoto Private Tour: Fushimi Inari, Kiyomizu-dera, the Old Lanes of Higashiyama & Gion
tour.subtitle: A private day in eastern Kyoto with a licensed guide and car: the tunnels of red torii gates at Fushimi Inari at opening time, Kiyomizu-dera on its wooden stage, the stone lanes of Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka, a kaiseki-style lunch, Kennin-ji temple and the geisha district of Gion at dusk.

highlights: Fushimi Inari's thousands of red torii gates, before the crowds
Kiyomizu-dera and its wooden stage above the trees
The stone-paved lanes of Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka
Kennin-ji, Kyoto's oldest Zen temple, and its twin dragons
Hanamikoji and Shirakawa in Gion, the geisha district
A licensed guide who explains etiquette and helps you behave respectfully
tour.overview:
Kyoto was the capital of Japan for more than a thousand years, from 794 to 1868, and the home of the emperors, the court and the great Buddhist sects. Spared from bombing in the Second World War, it kept some 1,600 temples and 400 shrines, wooden townhouses and gardens. Seventeen of its monuments form the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Historic Kyoto, inscribed in 1994.

This private day covers the eastern side of the city with a licensed guide and a car. You walk through the torii gates of Fushimi Inari at opening time, before the tour groups, see Kiyomizu-dera on its hillside, stroll through the lanes of Higashiyama, have a seasonal lunch, visit the Zen temple of Kennin-ji and end in Gion in the evening, when geiko and maiko may hurry to their appointments.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours 30 minutes
• Start and end: your hotel in Kyoto
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; about 8 km with many steps and slopes

WHAT YOU SEE
• Fushimi Inari Taisha and the Senbon Torii.
• Kiyomizu-dera.
• Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka.
• Yasaka shrine.
• Kennin-ji.
• Gion: Hanamikoji and Shirakawa.

WHY THIS WORKS
We start at Fushimi Inari at 7:30, when the gates are quiet and the light is soft, and leave Gion for the end of the afternoon, its most atmospheric time.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors to Kyoto, photographers and anyone who wants to understand the customs of temples, shrines and geisha.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer gardens and bamboo forests, choose our Kinkaku-ji and Arashiyama tour of western Kyoto.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
In Gion, photographing geiko and maiko without permission and walking in private alleys are forbidden and fined; your guide explains the rules. Kyoto is very crowded in cherry blossom and autumn colour seasons.

days.name: Fushimi Inari, Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka, Yasaka shrine, Kennin-ji and Gion
days.description:
What to expect: the great sights of eastern Kyoto from early morning to dusk, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 7:15 and drive to Fushimi Inari Taisha, the head shrine of Inari, the deity of rice, sake and prosperity, founded in 711. Behind the main halls begin the Senbon Torii, thousands of vermilion gates, each donated by a business or a family with its name painted on the back, forming tunnels up the sacred mountain. Stone foxes, Inari's messengers, hold keys and scrolls in their mouths. In the quiet of the morning you walk up to the Yotsutsuji crossroads, about 45 minutes, with a view over the city.

You drive to Kiyomizu-dera, the 'pure water temple', founded in 778. Its main hall stands on a huge wooden stage held up by 139 pillars, built without a single nail, above a valley of maple and cherry trees; the saying 'to jump off the stage of Kiyomizu' means to take a bold decision. You drink from the Otowa waterfall, whose three streams bring long life, success or love. Below the temple, you walk down Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka, stone-paved lanes of wooden houses with tea shops, pottery and pickle sellers, past the Yasaka pagoda.

After a seasonal lunch – tofu, yuba, small dishes of local vegetables – you visit Yasaka shrine at the head of Gion, then Kennin-ji, founded in 1202 as Kyoto's first Zen temple, with its raked gravel gardens, a screen of wind and thunder gods and, on the ceiling of the Dharma hall, two huge dragons painted in 2002. You end in Gion as the lanterns are lit, walking along Hanamikoji, lined with ochaya teahouses, and the willow-lined Shirakawa canal, where you might glimpse a maiko on her way to an engagement. Your driver takes you back to your hotel at about 16:30, or you can stay for dinner.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:15 – Pick-up at your hotel.
07:30 – Fushimi Inari (about 1 hour 45 minutes).
09:45 – Kiyomizu-dera.
11:00 – Sannenzaka, Ninenzaka and the Yasaka pagoda.
12:15 – Lunch.
13:30 – Yasaka shrine.
14:00 – Kennin-ji.
15:15 – Gion: Hanamikoji and Shirakawa.
16:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Some private lanes in Gion are closed to tourists, with fines for entering; your guide knows where you may go.
• A tea ceremony or a dinner with a maiko can be arranged on request.
• In spring and autumn we may start even earlier to beat the crowds.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Kiyomizu-dera and Kennin-ji tickets, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: tea ceremony, dinner, drinks with lunch.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Do we climb all of Fushimi Inari mountain?
faq.answer: No. We walk to the Yotsutsuji crossroads, about halfway, with a view over Kyoto. The full loop to the summit takes 2 to 3 hours and can be arranged.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: Kiyomizu-dera and Kennin-ji. Fushimi Inari and Yasaka shrine are free.

faq.question: Will we see a geisha?
faq.answer: Possibly, in Gion at dusk, but never guaranteed. A private dinner or tea with a maiko can be arranged in advance.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, a seasonal Kyoto lunch. Vegetarian diets are easy in Kyoto, home of temple cuisine.

faq.question: Is there much walking?
faq.answer: About 8 km with many steps and slopes. The car shortens the distances between areas.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the torii tunnels, the foxes and the waterfall. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The lower gates of Fushimi Inari, Yasaka shrine and Gion are flat; Kiyomizu-dera and the lanes are steep. Tell us your needs.

faq.question: Can we wear a kimono?
faq.answer: Yes. We can book a kimono rental near Kiyomizu-dera for the day.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not customary in Japan, and no one will expect it.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes easy to take off, and layers. Kyoto is very hot and humid in summer and cold in winter.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: Late March to early April for cherry blossom and mid-November to early December for autumn colours, both very busy. May and October are pleasant and calmer.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
